newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares close down, but not out.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares close down, but not out.

text.p: Danish share prices closed down on Tuesday, as expected after Monday's Wall Street falls, but with a decline of 0.48 percent they disproved fears of a profit-taking stampede after the closing highs of last week.
Dealers had earlier predicted a one or two percent drop.

The New York opening on Tuesday showed prices edging up, but Copenhagen dealers expected their market on Wednesday to be less influenced by Wall Street than by Danish food and drink group Danisco's 1996/97 results, due out during the day.
Analysts expect pre-tax profits up 12.7 percent year-on-year but the share closed four crowns down at 429.00.
The KFX top-20 index fell 0.83 point to 172.28 in overall bourse turnover of 1.66 billion crowns. The KFX August future fell 0.90 point to 172.60 with 50 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
BG Bank continued to fall following last week's Kleinwort Benson downgrade of its recommendation, to hold, and its characterisation of the share as overvalued.
The paper closed seven crowns down at 348.00. But Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark swam against the tide, rising four crowns to 630.63 and two crowns to 370.00 respectively.
